memories.memory: I privately support stronger public funding for independent artists and libraries, even though most of my relatives think government money should go to more practical services.
I stopped attending organized religious services regularly around 2018, but I still fast during Ramadan some years because the ritual helps me feel connected to my family and cultural background.

During a 2023 gallery project in Istanbul, I argued against removing a politically controversial painting because I believe discomfort is part of serious art, and the disagreement strained my relationship with the curator.
I tend to vote for candidates who defend secular government and freedom of expression, even when their economic policies are less favorable to people in my profession.
I donated about 2,000 Turkish lira in 2022 to a small local campaign supporting displaced artists, but I did not mention the donation when applying for a related arts grant.
I am uneasy with the idea that artistic institutions should publicly endorse every popular social cause, because I think creators need room to be contradictory and politically unfashionable.

My older brother and I still argue about immigration policy; I favor offering asylum to people fleeing war, while he believes the country should sharply restrict new arrivals because of pressure on housing and jobs.
